newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Coffee Board opposes call for brand name.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Coffee Board opposes call for brand name.

text.p: Kenya's coffee board remains opposed to marketing Kenya's coffee with a brand name, as favoured by some industry participants.
The board, the principal marketing agency, says in a policy document passed to Reuters at the weekend in Murang'a, central Kenya, that calls for a brand name were simply misguided.
A board spokesman said, "Around the world, it has been known that you blend Kenyan coffee to produce the particular taste one requires. Kenyan coffee as Kenyan coffee would miss those attributes."

"To maintain this (blending) leadership image, the board in conjuction with other players will continue to encourage farmers to enhance coffee yields and quality in order to consistently command premium prices and by implication enhanced financial returns to the farmer," the board said.
"This will be achieved through sustained support for research and through educational and promotional field services," the board policy document added.
The board spokesman said that it was not certain that a brand name, such as Kilimanjaro for Tanzanian coffee, would instantly ensure better sales or returns for the Kenyan beans.
The official also spoke out strongly against production of instant coffee in Kenya, saying it was not viable for export.
Japanese and American consumers have previously spoken in support of a brand name and list the success of Kilimanjaro as evidence that Kenyans have nothing to fear from such a name.
The board document pledged stepped up promotional efforts for Kenyan coffee in Eastern Europe countries, the Commonwealth of Independent States, Middle East and China.
It said as a step to enhance marketing, promotional materials would be developed and brochures would be available in hotels, restaurants and markets abroad on Kenyan coffee.
"Video tapes on Kenyan coffee will be produced and shown on major airlines (in promotion)," the document said.
"Kenya could market (sell) more coffee without driving down the world coffee price significantly," the document said.

The document, passed to Reuters during a visit to coffee fields in Murang'a, also said market intelligence pointed to a sharp growth in a gourmet market around the world and Kenya's focus must be to actively promote gourmet coffee to potential areas.
